title: Food contact materials: authorised substances
summary: EU authorises the use of multiple substances in plastic food contact materials from 18 November 2026
update:
The European Union (EU) has authorised the use of the following substances in the manufacture of plastic food contact materials (FCM):

chopped carbon fibres from carbonised polyacrylonitrile nano precipitated calcium carbonate, uncoated poly(2-hydroxypropanoic acid), n-octyl/n-decyl esters mixture of 1,9-nonanediamine (NMDA) and 2-methyl-1,8-octanediamine (MODA).

The authorisations include specifications on how and when these substances may be used.
why: The authorisation of substances for the manufacture of plastic FCM under Regulation 2026/2412 follows safety evaluations by the European Food Safety Authority (EFSA 2022a , 2022b , 2023 , 2024 ).
timeline: The substances newly authorised in Regulation 2026/2412 can be used from 18 November 2026 .
actions: Suppliers of packaged food to the EU market should inform packaging suppliers about upcoming changes in the authorised substances listed in Regulation 10/2011 , Annex I.
background:
Regulation 10/2011 specifies which substances may be used in plastic FCM, and establishes specific migration limits (SML) that limit their presence in food. For substances with no SML or other restrictions in Annex I, a generic SML of 60 mg/kg applies.

The Regulation also requires that materials and articles comply with specified quality and safety standards, and that they are labelled appropriately. The Regulation applies to all plastic materials and articles intended to come into contact with food, including packaging, containers, and utensils.
